$schema: Original rhymes and short song texts (CC BY 4.0), written for this project. Each line has a literal (word-for-word) and a natural translation. No third-party lyrics are bundled: the learner's own lyrics are stored only in their browser.

rhymes.title: La pioggia sul tetto
rhymes.summary: A cheerful rain rhyme: the cat sleeps, the wind sings, grandmother cooks soup.

lines.natural: It's raining, raining on the roof,
lines.note: piove: impersonal weather verb — no subject. sul = su + il.

lines.natural: the cat is asleep in bed.
lines.note: tetto / letto: rhyme on -etto.

lines.natural: The water falls gently, gently
lines.note: Verb before subject: common in poetry and with verbs like cadere. Doubling an adverb (piano piano) intensifies it.

lines.it: sulla strada e sul prato lontano.
lines.literal: on-the street and on-the meadow far.
lines.natural: on the street and the distant meadow.
lines.note: lontano agrees with prato (masculine singular).

lines.natural: The wind sings at the window,
lines.note: alla = a + la.

lines.natural: Grandma is making soup.
lines.note: finestra / minestra: rhyme on -estra.

lines.natural: It's raining, raining — what fun!
lines.note: che + noun = what (a) …!

lines.natural: tomorrow the cloud will go away.
lines.note: Present tense for the near future. andare via = to go away.

grammarNotes.title: Impersonal weather verbs
grammarNotes.text: piove = it rains / it is raining. Italian has no 'it' subject here.

grammarNotes.title: Subject after the verb
grammarNotes.text: Cade l'acqua, Canta il vento: the subject follows the verb, which gives a poetic rhythm.

grammarNotes.title: Articulated prepositions
grammarNotes.text: sul tetto, nel letto, sulla strada, alla finestra.

exercises.prompt: What does *piano piano* mean in 'Cade l'acqua piano piano'?
exercises.explanation: piano as an adverb = softly, slowly; doubling it intensifies.

exercises.prompt: Who is singing at the window?
exercises.explanation: Canta il vento alla finestra: il vento is the subject, placed after the verb.

exercises.prompt: Infinitive of *cade*?
exercises.explanation: cadere: cado, cadi, cade…

exercises.prompt: 'domani la nuvola va via' — when does the cloud go away?
exercises.explanation: The present tense with domani expresses the near future.

exercises.prompt: Complete the rhyme: il gatto dorme nel ___.
exercises.explanation: tetto / letto.

rhymes.title: Ninna nanna della luna
rhymes.summary: A mother sings her little bear to sleep under the moon and stars.

lines.natural: Sleep now, sleep, little bear,
lines.note: dormi here is an imperative (an instruction to tu). For -ere and -ire verbs the tu imperative is identical to the present: dormi = you sleep / sleep!

lines.natural: the moon is watching over the wood.
lines.note: guardare takes a direct object: no preposition for 'at'.

lines.natural: A star is shining in the sky,
lines.note: in cielo: no article in this fixed phrase.

lines.it: la notte è calma e bella.
lines.literal: the night is calm and beautiful.
lines.natural: the night is calm and lovely.
lines.note: stella / bella: rhyme on -ella. Both adjectives agree with notte (feminine).

lines.natural: The owl sings very softly,
morning is still far away.
lines.note: ancora = still. piano / lontano rhyme.

lines.it: Chiudi gli occhi, vicino al cuore:
lines.literal: Close the eyes, near to-the heart:
lines.natural: Close your eyes, close to my heart:
lines.note: chiudi: imperative of chiudere (same form as the present tu). gli occhi: Italian uses the article, not the possessive, for body parts.

lines.natural: Mummy sings to you with love.
lines.note: cuore / amore: the most traditional rhyme in Italian song.

grammarNotes.title: The tu imperative
grammarNotes.text: dormi! chiudi! For -ere and -ire verbs the tu imperative is identical to the present tense; for -are verbs it ends in -a (canta!). The full imperative, including the formal and negative forms, is in the imperativo lesson.

grammarNotes.title: Body parts with the article
grammarNotes.text: Chiudi gli occhi = close your eyes.

exercises.prompt: In *Dormi, dormi, piccolo orso*, what is *dormi*?
exercises.explanation: dormi is the tu imperative here (identical in form to the present tu).

exercises.prompt: What does *il giorno è ancora lontano* tell the little bear?
options: Morning is still a long way off.
exercises.answer: Morning is still a long way off.
exercises.explanation: ancora = still; lontano = far: it is still the middle of the night.

exercises.prompt: In *Brilla in cielo una stella*, what is the subject?
exercises.explanation: The subject follows the verb: una stella brilla.

exercises.prompt: Which word rhymes with *cuore* in the last couplet?
exercises.explanation: cuore / amore.

exercises.prompt: Translate naturally: *la notte è calma e bella*
exercises.answer: the night is calm and beautiful
accept: the night is calm and lovely
the night is quiet and beautiful
the night is quiet and lovely
exercises.explanation: calma and bella agree with notte.

rhymes.title: Conta delle stelle
rhymes.summary: Count from one to ten with stars, little owls and fish.

lines.natural: One star, two stars,
lines.note: uno → una before a feminine noun; stella → stelle.

lines.natural: three stars, so very pretty.
lines.note: belle agrees with stelle (feminine plural).

lines.natural: Four, five, six and seven:

lines.it: sul tetto ci sono le civette.
lines.literal: on-the roof there are the little-owls.
lines.natural: there are little owls on the roof.
lines.note: ci sono + plural. sette / civette rhyme.

lines.natural: Eight, nine, ten:
in the sea the fish are sleeping.
lines.note: Subject after the verb. dieci / pesci rhyme by assonance.

lines.natural: Good night, lovely stars,
see you tomorrow, dear sisters!
lines.note: a domani = see you tomorrow. care: feminine plural of caro.

grammarNotes.title: Plural of -a nouns
grammarNotes.text: stella → stelle; civetta → civette; sorella → sorelle.

grammarNotes.title: ci sono
grammarNotes.text: sul tetto ci sono le civette = there are little owls on the roof.

exercises.prompt: Match the numbers.
exercises.explanation: uno, due, tre, quattro, cinque, sei, sette, otto, nove, dieci.

exercises.prompt: Where are the little owls?
exercises.explanation: sul tetto ci sono le civette.

exercises.prompt: Plural of *la civetta*: le ___
What does *a domani* mean?
exercises.explanation: a domani is a common way to say goodbye until the next day.

exercises.prompt: Why *care sorelle* and not *cari sorelle*?
exercises.explanation: The adjective agrees: caro → care (feminine plural).

rhymes.title: Il valzer degli animali
rhymes.summary: Animals dance on the roof, in bed and in the meadow; the owl challenges everyone.

lines.natural: The cat is dancing on the roof,
lines.note: Verb–subject order for rhythm.

lines.natural: the mouse is dancing on the bed.

lines.it: La rana salta, la lumaca è lenta,
lines.literal: The frog jumps, the snail is slow,
lines.natural: The frog jumps, the snail is slow,

lines.it: la farfalla vola ed è contenta.
lines.literal: the butterfly flies and is happy.
lines.natural: the butterfly flies and is happy.
lines.note: ed: e before a vowel (here è). lenta / contenta rhyme.

lines.natural: The owl sings: “One, two, three!

lines.it: Chi balla più veloce di me?»
lines.literal: Who dances more fast than me?”
lines.natural: Who can dance faster than me?”
lines.note: più … di = more … than; di + stressed pronoun me. tre / me rhyme.

lines.natural: All together, nice and slow,

lines.it: balliamo il valzer, mano nella mano.
lines.literal: we-dance the waltz, hand in-the hand.
lines.natural: let's dance the waltz, hand in hand.
lines.note: balliamo: noi form, here a suggestion (let's dance). mano nella mano = hand in hand.

grammarNotes.title: Comparison
grammarNotes.text: più veloce di me = faster than me.

exercises.prompt: What does the owl ask?
exercises.explanation: Chi balla più veloce di me?

exercises.prompt: Infinitive of *vola*?
exercises.explanation: volare: volo, voli, vola…

exercises.prompt: *mano nella mano* means…
options: in the hand of the waltz
exercises.explanation: nella = in + la.

exercises.prompt: Why does the text say *ed è contenta* instead of *e è contenta*?
options: e becomes ed before a vowel, especially e
ed is the feminine of e
exercises.answer: e becomes ed before a vowel, especially e
exercises.explanation: The euphonic d avoids two identical vowels in a row.

exercises.prompt: ballare, noi: ___
exercises.explanation: ball- + -iamo.
